MUJAHID:v2p682/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p682/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p682/r1.claim: Mujahid says a person of means should spend according to his means on the divorced woman if she nurses his child.

MUQATIL:65:6-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:65:6-7/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:65:6-7/r3.claim: A wealthy person spends according to wealth; someone whose provision is constricted spends according to what God gave, as qadara means constrict in 21:87.

MUQATIL:65:6-7/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:65:6-7/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:65:6-7/r4.claim: God does not burden a person beyond what He provided and will bring abundance after poverty and hardship.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p471#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p471#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p471#2/r1.claim: Qudira ʿalayhi rizquhu means his provision has been made tight or restricted.

TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r1.claim: A well-off former husband pays from his means for his ex-wife's nursing and their young child; a man with restricted provision pays according to what God gave him.

TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī glosses ample means as one's available wealth and constrained provision as being given little.

TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r3.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r3.claim: Sufyān explains spending from one's means as spending according to one's capacity.

TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the required payment is set according to what the man can find.

TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the spending is owed to the divorced woman if she nurses the man's child.

TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v23p68#2/r6.claim: ʿUmar sent Abū ʿUbayda a thousand dinars and, after he used them for finer clothes and food, said he had rightly applied the verse on spending according to means.

TAB-FULL:v23p70/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r1.claim: God requires spending on dependents only within the provision He has given, according to each person's means; the poor are not held to the rich person's obligation.

TAB-FULL:v23p70/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says God does not charge the poor with the same burden as the rich.

TAB-FULL:v23p70/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r3.speaker: هشيم
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r3.claim: Hushaym glosses God's limit as what He has made obligatory.

TAB-FULL:v23p70/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r4.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r4.claim: Sufyān interprets the limit as what a person can afford.

TAB-FULL:v23p70/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p70/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God does not demand charity or zakat from someone who has nothing to give or purify.

ZAJJAJ:v5p186/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p186/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p186/r4.claim: The affluent should provide nursing mothers according to their means; someone with only subsistence should spend accordingly, as the rule for the affluent and constrained states.

ZAJJAJ:v5p186/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p186/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p186/r5.claim: The clause “what He has given her” means what God has bestowed upon her.

ZAJJAJ:v5p187/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p187/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p187/r1.claim: Most Muslims were poor and needy in the Prophet’s time; God promised relief, and later opened conquests brought ease after hardship.

NAHHAS:v4p453/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p453/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p453/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says one with household goods to sell should sell them and spend the proceeds.

NAHHAS:v4p453/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p453/r11.speaker: السدي
NAHHAS:v4p453/r11.claim: Al-Suddī says God does not burden a poor person with a rich person's spending.

NAHHAS:v4p453/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p453/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v4p453/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says a poor person is not required to pay zakat or charity.

NAHHAS:v4p453/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p453/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p453/r13.claim: God gives ease after hardship in this world or the next, encouraging believers to do good.

NAHHAS:v4p453/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p453/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p453/r8.claim: The imperative lām is normally kasra but is silent after fa in falyunfiq; kasra is also allowed.

NAHHAS:v4p453/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p453/r9.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p453/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows the reading that a constrained person spends according to the limits of his provision.

THALABI:v9p341#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p341#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p341#2/r1.claim: A person with means should spend in proportion to their wealth; someone whose provision is constrained should spend from what God has granted.

THALABI:v9p341#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p341#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p341#2/r2.claim: God does not require expenditure beyond the wealth He has given a person.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r20.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r20.claim: God requires the father to pay the nurse only according to his means.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r21.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r21.claim: A person is not required to give charity or zakat when he has no wealth subject to charity or zakat.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r22.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r22.claim: Obligation is limited to the capacity God has granted a person.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p33/r23.claim: Ease after hardship may mean abundance after constriction or ability after incapacity.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p516/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p516/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p516/r3.claim: A person of means must provide according to his means, while one whose provision is limited spends according to that limit, as in 2:236.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p516/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p516/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p516/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says God does not burden a poor person with what He requires of a rich person; that would require what was never given.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p517/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p517/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p517/r1.claim: Ease after hardship means wealth and abundance after constraint and difficulty.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p517/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p517/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p517/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq says most people then were poor, but God promised ease, later opening prosperity for Muslims; believers in hardship can hope for God's relief.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:65:7-9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:65:7-9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:65:7-9/r1.claim: People with means must provide for their nursing wives according to their means; someone whose resources are only subsistence spends accordingly.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:65:7-9/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:65:7-9/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:65:7-9/r2.claim: God does not overburden a person beyond what He gave; despite their poverty, believers would receive ease and expanded provision after hardship, as happened later.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p157/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p157/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p157/r1.claim: A person of means should spend in proportion to their means; one whose provision is restricted spends from what God gave. God imposes no spending beyond that provision and brings ease after hardship.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p560/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p560/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p560/r10.claim: God makes the affairs and knots of a person who acts by these rulings in piety easier; observing the specified housing, non-harm, support, and nursing-wage duties earns forgiveness and great reward.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r2.claim: The wealthy should spend according to their means and the constrained should be moderate; this is fair because the woman is not left destitute and the man is not burdened beyond capacity.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r3.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو هريرة وابن المسيب والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r3.claim: Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, Isḥāq, Abū Hurayra, Ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Ḥasan say a husband unable to support his wife is separated from her; jurists of opinion and others say there is no separation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p326/r4.claim: The promise of ease consoles people; most read yaʿẓumu, while al-Aʿmash reads naʿẓimu in the first-person plural.

TABRISI:65:7-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:65:7-10/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:65:7-10/r1.claim: God will bring ease after hardship, wealth after poverty, and relief after difficulty; this consoled impoverished Companions before later conquests.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r1.claim: The Prophet referred Hind to what sufficed her, based on Abu Sufyan’s means, rather than imposing a fixed amount; the verse itself does not establish fixed rates.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r10.speaker: محمد بن المواز
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r10.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Mawwaz says both parents owe child support in proportion to their inheritance shares; Ibn al-Arabi suggests he may mean the mother only when no father exists.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r11.claim: A report lists a wife, an enslaved worker, and a child each asking the addressee to provide for them, with the child asking who else will support him.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r2.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r2.claim: Umar assigned a newborn a monthly allowance of one hundred dirhams, while Uthman assigned fifty; Ibn al-Arabi suggests prices or circumstances may explain the difference.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن هلال المزني
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r3.claim: He reports from his father and grandmother that Uthman sent a newborn fifty dirhams and a garment, promising to raise the grant to one hundred after a year.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r4.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r4.claim: Ali assigned a foundling an allowance of one hundred dirhams.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says scholars differ whether support before weaning is recommended or obligatory; he holds it obligatory and says its amount varies with circumstances at birth and weaning.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r6.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r6.claim: Sufyan ibn Wahb reports that Umar set each Muslim a monthly ration of two mudd of wheat and one qist each of vinegar and oil.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda praises the practices Umar established for Muhammad’s community as rightly guided.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r8.claim: The Syrian mudd and qist measures have changed; support includes customary food and clothing, adjusted to circumstances and local custom.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#2/r9.claim: The verse establishes that a father, rather than the mother, must support a child.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#3/r1.claim: The Qur’an and Sunnah reinforce the same rule about a person’s responsibility to provide for dependents.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7#3/r2.claim: God does not charge a poor person as He charges a wealthy one; hardship is followed by wealth and greater ease.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r1.claim: A husband supports his wife and young child according to his means; a well-off provider gives more, while a poor one gives what he can.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r2.claim: Under the author’s view, a judge or mufti estimates support from both the recipient’s need and the provider’s means, guided by customary living standards.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r3.speaker: الشافعي وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r3.claim: Shafi‘i and his companions hold that maintenance is fixed solely by the husband’s means, without regard to the wife’s means or sufficiency; they prescribe two, one-and-a-half, or one mudd.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r4.speaker: الشافعي وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r4.claim: They argue that measuring support by need is unknowable and invites disputes, so a caliph’s daughter and a guard’s daughter receive the same amount.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r5.claim: Qurtubi answers that the verse establishes differences between rich and poor husbands but does not exclude the wife’s condition from customary support.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r6.claim: The command to provide according to recognized custom applies to both spouses; customary support for a wealthy woman is not the same as for a poor woman.

QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:65:7/r7.claim: The Prophet told Hind to take what adequately supported her and her child according to custom.

BAYDAWI-FULL:65:7-10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:65:7-10/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:65:7-10/r1.claim: Wealthy and constrained people each spend according to their means; God charges only what He has granted, consoling the poor and promising ease soon and in the afterlife.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r1.claim: Every affluent or constrained person should spend according to his means; this concerns provision for divorced women and nursing mothers.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r2.claim: A constrained provision is a narrow amount allotted by God in proportion to one's capacity; God does not require beyond the provision He gave.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p257/r3.claim: God promises ease after hardship to the person in straitened circumstances.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p200/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p200/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p200/r7.claim: Because divorce involves aversion, husbands may slander former wives to discourage suitors; repeated calls to piety press them to obey the law, respect rights, avoid harm, and pay maintenance, earning expiation and reward.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r1.claim: A well-off or constrained husband should spend according to his capacity on divorced women and nursing mothers; no one is required to spend beyond what God has given.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r2.claim: The apparent addressee is the husband, making this a basis for the father's duty to maintain a child rather than the mother's.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن المواز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r3.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Mawwāz says both parents contribute to a child's maintenance in proportion to their inheritance shares.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r4.claim: He cites a report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī in which a son says, “My father, support me; to whom will you leave me?”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r5.claim: Most read لينفق with the imperative lām; Abū Muʿādh reports a purpose lām with subjunctive, governed by an omitted “we prescribed this.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r6.claim: Most read قدر with a light dāl; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads it doubled.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r7.claim: The promise that God will make ease after hardship means a person whose provision is restricted will receive openings in provision; it is not limited to poor people at the time or poor husbands.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة والحسن وابن المسيب ومالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r8.claim: They say that if a husband pays what he can but cannot maintain his wife, the couple is separated.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r9.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p202#2/r9.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and a group say the couple is not separated for inability to provide maintenance.

SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r1.claim: The common لينفق has a jussive verb governed by the imperative lām.

SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r2.speaker: أبو معاذ القارئ
SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r2.claim: Abu Muadh al-Qari reads the verb in the subjunctive under a purpose lām, with an implicit أن and an implied clause meaning this was prescribed so he would spend.

SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:65:7/r3.claim: The common قدر is light; Ibn Abi Ubayla reads it with doubling.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r1.claim: A child’s father or guardian should spend according to his means; God does not burden a person beyond what He gives, as another verse says.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r2.claim: Umar tested how Abu Ubayda would use a thousand dinars; seeing that he then wore better clothes and ate better food, Umar said Abu Ubayda had rightly applied this verse.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r3.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p153#2/r3.claim: A Prophetic report compares three people giving one tenth of their very different wealth and says their rewards are equal; Ibn Kathir calls this route unusual.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r1.claim: God promises relief after hardship and does not break His promise, as the two verses in al-Sharh repeat.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r2.claim: In a report, a destitute wife reassures her hungry returning husband that provision is coming; her oven fills with goat meat and the mill turns. The Prophet said the mill would have continued had she left it alone.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p154/r3.claim: A second report tells of a poor couple whose mill and cooking vessel fill after the wife prays; the Prophet says the untouched mill would have kept turning until Resurrection.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r1.claim: Fear of poverty is no excuse to withhold support: the well-provided should be generous, while the constrained must give according to their means and trust God.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r2.claim: “Restricted in provision” means God has limited a person to necessities; the passive wording teaches proper reverence in speaking of God’s action.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r3.claim: Support is required for nursing women and others whom God obligates, and spending only a portion of what He gave does not consume the whole gift.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r4.claim: God may replace support from capital, household goods, or sale of property when income is unavailable; the Prophet exemplifies simplicity and ease.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r5.claim: God does not burden a soul beyond what He has provided; the verse may imply that a person given a duty to spend receives means to meet it.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r6.claim: God promises ease after hardship, though not necessarily after every hardship; no one remains restricted throughout every circumstance of life.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r7.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r7.claim: Al-Qushayrī says expecting relief marks those of intermediate spiritual rank: they rise above despair but have not reached contentment whether means are present or absent.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p35/r8.claim: The promise was plainly fulfilled for the Companions, who gained Arabia, Persia, and Byzantium and their treasures; its promise remains enduring.

DURR-FULL:v8p206/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p206/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p206/r12.claim: Mujahid applies spending according to means to a divorced woman who nurses for the father.

DURR-FULL:v8p206/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p206/r13.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p206/r13.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses constrained provision as restricted, and what God has given as what He granted.

DURR-FULL:v8p208/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r1.claim: Umar sent Abu Ubayda money after learning he dressed and ate austerely; when Abu Ubayda used it for comfort, Umar said he had applied the command to spend according to one's means.

DURR-FULL:v8p208/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r2.claim: A weak report says a believer taught by God spends generously when given abundance and restricts spending when provision is restricted.

DURR-FULL:v8p208/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r3.claim: The Prophet says three donors who each gave one tenth of their wealth receive equal reward, whatever the size of their wealth.

DURR-FULL:v8p208/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r4.claim: Abu Malik al-Ashari transmits the same teaching: donors of one tenth of their differing fortunes are equal in reward.

DURR-FULL:v8p208/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r5.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v8p208/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri says an unable husband should be given time rather than separated from his wife, citing that God burdens each only within what He granted; Ma'mar says Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz agreed.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r1.claim: Every affluent or constrained person must spend according to their means, even if the amount is small; the command apparently addresses fathers.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r10.claim: The promise of ease after hardship may encourage the poor of an endowment, or spouses who spend what they can without negligence; the clause stands independently only on the first reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi treats the verse as the basis for a father's duty to provide maintenance.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r3.speaker: محمد بن المواز
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Mawwaz disagrees, assigning the duty to both parents in proportion to inheritance shares.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r4.speaker: أبو معاذ
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r4.claim: Abu Muʿadh reports a reading with purpose lām and an accusative ق, understood as God legislating this so the person would spend.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r5.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r5.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads قدر with a doubled dāl.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r6.claim: God burdens a person only according to the capacity or wealth He has granted, whether little or much; the wording comforts the poor person.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r7.speaker: عبد العزيز وأبو حنيفة وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r7.claim: They infer that inability to maintain a wife does not allow the marriage to be annulled.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة والحسن وابن المسيب ومالك والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r8.claim: They hold that inability to provide maintenance dissolves the marriage and separates the spouses.

ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r9.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v28p140/r9.claim: Al-Suyuti derives a recommendation to match spending and charity to one's circumstances, quoting a report that believers imitate God's measured giving.

ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r10.claim: God does not require anyone to give beyond what He has granted; the wealthy and poor are each obligated according to their means, and someone able to borrow may do so in good faith with later repayment.

ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r11.claim: God will create ease after hardship; poor families should be patient with what they can find and retain hope, while the rich should not neglect them but support them with zakat, alms, and aid.

ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r12.claim: Disorder in family and financial matters, immorality, mismanagement, disobedience, injustice, and excess can bring the collapse of a society, civilization, or country; the sura links back to al-Taghabun and forward to al-Tahrim.

ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r7.claim: Anyone required to provide maintenance must spend according to their means, neither giving their entire wealth nor overburdening themselves.

ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r8.claim: The well-off should spend from their abundance with moderation, neither extravagantly nor restrictively, following the balanced spending praised in al-Furqan.

ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:65:2-7#5/r9.claim: Those whose livelihood is restricted should give according to what God has provided, with middle-income people giving moderately and the poor little.

ELMALILI:65:2-7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:65:2-7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:65:2-7/r1.claim: The author renders the rule as the affluent spending according to their means and the constrained spending from God's provision; no soul is charged beyond what it has received, and hardship is followed by ease.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r1.claim: Here spending means providing the necessities of life, including food and clothing.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r10.claim: The instruction that God burdens no soul beyond what He gives explains the order to spend according to one's means and had already been established in 2:286.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r2.claim: The first من is source or origin: spending issues from one's means; unlike the partitive من in 8:3 and later in this verse, expenditure is not a portion of one's capacity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r3.claim: Unlike the من in this verse, the من in 8:3 is partitive because spending is a portion of one's provision; here the second من is also partitive.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r4.claim: A restricted provision is limited means; whoever is financially constrained should spend within what they can afford, observing priorities and levels of duty.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r5.claim: He cites the Prophet's instruction to Hind, Abu Sufyan's wife, to take from her husband's property what suffices for her and her child according to recognized custom.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r6.claim: Recognized custom is ordinary social practice unless Islamic law overrides it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r7.claim: Provision includes useful necessities such as food, clothing, goods, and housing, whether supplied as objects or money; it often means food specifically.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r8.claim: Scholars agree support has no fixed amount because circumstances, times, and places differ; they dispute how much an affluent provider owes beyond sufficiency.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p330/r9.claim: He treats the disagreement over extra provision as a difference in people's conditions and customs, requiring attention to the dependent's circumstances and accustomed standard.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r1.claim: This principle reassures the recipient not to demand more than the provider can afford; an insolvent provider who can feed and clothe dependents modestly without harm is not separated from them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r2.claim: What God has given includes earning ability, so a capable provider can be compelled to work to support dependents or supplement inadequate means.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r3.claim: If a person cannot earn and has nothing to spend, support for that person and dependents falls to the Muslims' public treasury according to its obligations.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r4.claim: Umar asks whether he should abandon a herdsman whose small flock has perished when the herdsman brings proof and appeals to the commander; Malik reports it in the Muwatta.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r5.claim: Jurists disagree whether a wife may seek separation when her husband cannot provide: Malik allows it after a waiting period, estimated here at two months; Abu Hanifa does not, with support instead from the treasury.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p331/r6.claim: If the public treasury functions, it must support indigent spouses; if support cannot be obtained there, the judge should separate them rather than leave the wife in need.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r1.claim: The promise of ease completes the preceding conclusion and encourages hope for dependents facing hardship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r2.claim: The statement means that God sometimes brings ease after hardship, so a distressed person may hope for relief; it does not promise every distressed person an end to hardship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r3.claim: He rejects forced readings that make this a universal promise to the Muslims of that time or to all compliant spenders, since experience can contradict them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r4.claim: The indefinite forms عسر and يسرا avoid suggesting the totality that definite forms could imply; he compares the wording in 94:5.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r5.claim: The legal rulings of divorce are followed by encouragement to obey through promises of escape, ease, forgiveness, and reward.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p332/r6.claim: Warnings about violating God's limits and the final warning about peoples who ignored God and His messengers guard against treating the legal duties lightly.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p413/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p413/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p413/r3.claim: This reading reconciles the verse with the general promise that God will bring ease after hardship in al-Talaq; the intervals can vary.

TABATABAI:65:6-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:65:6-7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:65:6-7/r4.claim: A person of means should expand support for his divorced wife nursing their child; someone with constrained means supports her according to what he can afford.

TABATABAI:65:6-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:65:6-7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:65:6-7/r5.claim: God burdens each person only within the capacity He has given, removing hardship from divine obligations including support for a divorced wife.

TABATABAI:65:6-7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:65:6-7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:65:6-7/r6.claim: The promise that ease will follow hardship offers reassurance and consolation.

TABATABAI:65:7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:65:7/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:65:7/r2.claim: A husband who divorces a pregnant woman supports her until delivery and then pays nursing wages; she has first claim to nurse until weaning unless she accepts the pay of a cheaper nurse.

TABATABAI:65:7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:65:7/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:65:7/r3.claim: If the husband provides enough to sustain her and clothing, they remain together; otherwise they are separated, according to a report on the constrained provider's duty.

TABATABAI:65:7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:65:7/r7.speaker: فاطمة بنت قيس
TABATABAI:65:7/r7.claim: Fatima bint Qays reports that after a final divorce the Prophet said she had no maintenance and let her move; she argues the home-retention rule is for revocable divorces, then describes the waiting periods and the requirement of two just witnesses for return.

ASAD-NOTES:65:7#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:65:7#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:65:7#n15/r1.claim: The phrase literally means spending 'out of' one's means.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p357/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p357/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p357/r1.claim: Taghābun warns that love of wife and children can become a trial: it may make a person shirk spending his life and wealth for God and turn family friendship into self-harm.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p357/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p357/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p357/r2.claim: Vigilance does not require severing family ties; one should forgive and forbear as far as possible, reforming relatives while protecting oneself from harm.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p358/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p358/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p358/r4.claim: Those who observe God’s limits despite financial hardship to please Him receive special aid; those who violate them from greed only wrong themselves.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r28.claim: The passage presents piety, reliance on God, measured responsibility, forgiveness, reward, and hope after hardship as general principles for believers facing divorce and life's other trials.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r29.claim: Believers should seek God's help after making a just effort, accept the outcome without clinging to preconceptions, and trust that God can provide material or spiritual relief unexpectedly.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r31.claim: Spending obligations, voluntary aid, and personal expenses must reflect a person's means; wealth does not justify waste, and spending should remain measured.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r32.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r32.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r32.claim: Limited means should not produce habitual stinginess or complaint: people should use what they have well, strive lawfully for more, and remain patient and hopeful.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r33.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r33.claim: God does not burden anyone beyond what He has given or beyond their capacity; hardship must be met with patience and effort.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r34.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r34.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r34.claim: The promise of ease after hardship is not a guarantee of immediate relief in every worldly crisis; the indefinite nouns encourage perseverance and hope, ultimately grounded in afterlife reward.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:65:1/r7.claim: Divorce is a serious civil act with responsibilities: it should follow rational and conscientious judgment, not fleeting impulses, and separation does not justify treating a spouse as an enemy.

QIRAAT-ER:65:7:28#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:65:7:28#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:65:7:28#1/r1.claim: Ḍamma on sīn rather than sukūn gives a fuller pronunciation with no semantic change.

QIRAAT-ER:65:7:29#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:65:7:29#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:65:7:29#1/r1.claim: Ḍamma on sīn parallels ʿusurin and maintains vowel harmony in the pair.

STUDYQURAN:65:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:65:7/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:65:7/r1.claim: Some interpret the husband’s payment to his former wife as depending on both her needs and his circumstances.

STUDYQURAN:65:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:65:7/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:65:7/r2.claim: Others say the amount paid to the former wife should be limited to her immediate needs.

STUDYQURAN:65:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:65:7/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:65:7/r3.claim: The verse is also taken as evidence that the husband alone must provide for the child, whether the couple remains married or is divorced.

STUDYQURAN:65:7/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:65:7/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:65:7/r4.claim: If these obligations are difficult, God will ease circumstances either by providing means in this life or by easing one’s way into the Garden for observing His command despite hardship.
